title: Opt-in type-aware lint path
caption: How an opted-in mixed TSRX and TypeScript project reaches one type-aware process without writing generated source to the project.

nodes.tsrx: Authored TSRX enters the separate type-aware project lane only when type-aware linting or type checking is enabled.
nodes.scan: TSRX reuses the shared structural scan before building its type-semantic projection.
nodes.projection: This projection preserves types, bindings, imports, control flow, and component callability while emitting legal TypeScript and TSX.
nodes.ordinary: Ordinary TypeScript and TSX can join the project batch without going through the TSRX scanner or projection.
nodes.config: Rules and path-sensitive overrides resolve against each authored file name before TSRX gets a virtual script identity.
nodes.batch: The complete mixed project is held in memory. TSRX uses a virtual .tsrx.tsx name and no generated file is written to the project.
nodes.tsgolint: One documented protocol-v2 tsgolint process receives the whole project batch through standard input.
nodes.mapping: Path-aware messages identify their source file, and safe fixes must cover one exact authored identity range.
nodes.spans: Labels and applicable fixes finish on the original TSRX spans. Edited TSRX is rescanned and reparsed before write.
